transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-22
Start: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Liam Patel (Redwood AE), Sofia Morales (Redwood SE), Rashid Khan (NovaEdge Head of Partnerships), Elena Rossi (NovaEdge Cloud Engineer), Priya Mehta (Product), Samir Das (Security)

Summary (auto):
Quick technical sync between Redwood and NovaEdge to align on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for a joint listing, and next steps for a staged deployment on NovaEdge infra. Discussed VPC connectivity, auth/SAML, data residency, and perf expectations. Agreed to share docs and schedule staging demo.

Topics: marketplace listing checklist; reference architecture (VPC, peering, auth); packaging and billing integration; security and compliance; staging perf tests

00:00 Liam: okay good morning everyone, uh this is Liam from Redwood, im joined by Sofia our SE, and we wanted to walk through the marketplace integration and the reference arch so we can get a staging deployment going.
00:18 Rashid: morning, yeah thanks. We spoke with product and cloud eng, we want to get the listing live in mid May if possible. Timeline a bit aggressive but doable.
00:28 Sofia: great, can you confirm the primary goals — is this purely a marketplace listing for visibility or do you want a joint reference architecture + deployment support?
00:38 Priya: for us it's both, we want the listing + a reference arch that shows how customers run Redwood on NovaEdge with VPC peering and managed marketplace billing. Also a short how-to for our docs portal.
00:51 Liam: perfect. high-level plan: we share our marketplace checklist, you provide network details and security contacts, SE sets up a staging deployment, run perf smoke tests, and then we coordinate the listing assets.
01:05 Elena: couple of practical Qs — network: NovaEdge runs dedicated tenant VPCs, support cross-account peering and private endpoints. We need to know what endpoints Redwood requires and port/egress.
01:16 Sofia: for hosted modes we normally use public endpoints, but for Dedicated/Private marketplace flows you'll want either VPC peering or private link. For the reference arch we'll produce diagrams for both. Required: control-plane API endpoint (HTTPS 443), optional metrics/agent egress to our monitoring, and kv cache traffic if you host a side-cache — not sure you'll need that though.
01:40 Samir: quick security note — we need encryption at rest, KMS integration, and audit logs. Does Redwood support customer-managed keys in the marketplace flow or only in Private deployments?
01:51 Sofia: good question. We currently support CMKs (customer-managed keys) for Private and Dedicated customers. Marketplace-lising typically uses our hosted offering but we can offer a Private variant as a marketplace product with extra steps — that requires a separate SOW. We'll document both options in the reference arch.
02:09 Rashid: ok sounds good. about billing integration: can customers purchase via NovaEdge marketplace and have usage metered back to Redwood so they pay Redwood and we get revenue share?
02:22 Liam: yes — we have partner marketplace billing integrations. Typically the marketplace handles purchase and we report usage via a partner billing API. We'll share the integration docs but note that metering granularity is token-based and per-model metrics matter for pricing.
02:39 Priya: do you have sample listing assets for the NovaEdge portal? imagery, short blurb, tags, categories?
02:48 Liam: yes i'll share a sample package — title, short 2-line summary, long description, logos (SVG/PNG), and link to the reference arch. We'll also share suggested keywords and supported regions.
02:58 Elena: on the networking again — one of our constraints is that some customers are in regulated regions and they require data not to leave region. Can the reference arch show region-restricted deployment patterns?
03:12 Sofia: absolutely, we'll include a regional deployment pattern with on-prem or VPC-only flows. There might be tradeoffs on latency and cost, we'll call those out. We'll also show KV cache placement and how prefix caching reduces token costs.
03:30 Rashid: any competitors we should call out in the listing? customers sometimes ask comparisons to CloudForge and EdgeStream.
03:38 Liam: we can include a small comparison note, but marketing usually keeps it neutral. I'll include factual differentiators: unified runtime, cost controls, and private deployment options.
03:50 Samir: curious about auth — SSO, SAML, SCIM provisioning. For enterprise buyers we often require SAML and a SCIM-based provisioning flow. Does Redwood support that out of the box?
04:03 Sofia: yes SAML SSO and SCIM are supported; RBAC at the org and route level is available. We'll include steps for enabling SSO via the marketplace listing and which claims we need. Some of the field names in the marketplace UI are odd, transcription sometimes says S A M L as S A M L, but that's fine.
04:22 Priya: for the reference architecture diagram can you include the minimum network ports and an example IAM/KMS mapping?
04:30 Sofia: yes we'll provide a diagram and an appendix with ports: 443 outbound for control plane, 22 only for admin if you allow SSH, optional 8080 for internal metrics — we'll list them precisely.
04:44 Elena: great. about deployment type — would we recommend Redwood Dedicated on NovaEdge or the hosted API with VPC peering? Which is simpler?
04:56 Sofia: hosted with private link is the fastest to market; dedicated provides better predictable throughput and isolation but needs infra provisioning. For a marketplace listing, the private-hosted option often fits most customers. We'll present both in the doc with pros/cons and estimated lead times.
05:15 Rashid: Perf and scale — if we list a reference arch, customers will ask about latency numbers. Can we run a quick smoke perf on a subset of models in staging to capture baseline latency at 512 tokens?
05:28 Liam: yes SE can run a smoke test. Sofia, can you run a 1-hour baseline test on NovaEdge staging once we have network peering?
05:35 Sofia: yes, we can run that. We'll test an open LLM variant (quantized) and a larger hosted variant to show delta. Note the transcription may mis-spell KV cache as K V cache, but we'll ignore that.
05:52 Priya: also we'd like a one-page integration guide for our docs portal. Could you make a condensed step-by-step for our devs?
05:59 Liam: yes we'll provide a condensed how-to and a full reference architecture.
06:05 Samir: compliance — we need SOC 2, ISO 27001 evidence and penetration test summaries. Do you have those ready?
06:13 Sofia: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and ISO docs; we'll share the security pack and a redacted pentest summary. For KMS we support AWS KMS / customer-managed keys in Dedicated/Private. For marketplace hosted listings, we can document controls and offer add-on options.
06:32 Elena: can you send the security pack link in the followup email?
06:36 Liam: yes i'll attach it.
06:40 Rashid: on the timeline again — if we got checklist and network details by EOW, can we get a staging demo the following week?
06:49 Liam: thats realistic. proposed dates in next steps.
06:54 10:07 Sofia: (technical) when we set up peering we'll need a service account for deployment with least privilege. We'll send a sample IAM policy. Also for KV caching if NovaEdge wants an in-cluster sidecar we'll include instructions — otherwise we use Redwood-managed cache.
07:18 Elena: sidecar would be interesting to reduce egress costs, can you outline tradeoffs?
07:25 Sofia: tradeoffs: sidecar reduces egress and can lower per-token cost, but increases infra responsibilities (updates, scaling). Managed cache is simpler but may incur egress charges and higher latency in some regions. We'll include cost estimates.
07:45 Rashid: any pitfalls you've seen with marketplace listings historically?
07:51 Liam: common pitfalls: missing network diagrams, unclear billing flows, and incomplete security docs. Also images/branding not sized correctly. We'll send a checklist to avoid those.
08:03 Priya: good — also can you include a reference terraform module example for peering and IAM? That would speed up our engineers.
08:13 Sofia: yes we'll include a minimal terraform snippet in the reference arch. Might be a small mis-typo in the transcript here but we'll ensure code is clean.
08:27 Elena: ok lets talk about the actual assets: screenshots, diagrams, logos. We can provide logos but need your accepted format.
08:36 Liam: svg and png high-res preferred, and a 1-line/2-line blurb plus a 200-400 word description. We'll provide exact specs in the checklist.
08:48 Rashid: last thing on integrations — do you support webhook callbacks for usage events? We need to capture events for internal chargeback.
08:57 Sofia: we have webhook endpoints and a partner metering API. We'll include sample payloads. There can be slight variations in field names in the transcript (e.g., "metering api" appearing as "metering apI"), but the docs will be clear.
09:15 Liam: all right to recap: Redwood to send marketplace checklist, sample listing assets, security pack, and reference architecture. NovaEdge to send VPC diagram, compliance contact, and confirm staging date. SE to run perf smoke once peering is up.
09:33 Priya: thanks, we'll aim to have VPC details by Sunday and confirm the staging slot.
09:38 Liam: perfect, i'll follow up with an email and attachments. any final questions?
09:44 Samir: none from me.
09:46 Elena: none.
09:48 Rashid: good meeting, thanks everyone.
09:51 Liam: thanks all, we'll talk soon. Bye.

Resources mentioned (links in followup): marketplace checklist (doc), reference architecture diagram (attachment), security pack (link), terraforming sample repo (github link), perf test plan (sheet).

End of transcript.
